Allocate land use change

Source: R/allocate.R
allocate.Rd

Allocation places the projected quantity of change on the map: for each period, it turns the land use at the start of the period (the anterior map) into the land use at its end (the posterior map), given the transition potentials and the demanded transition rates.

allocate() runs a contiguous sequence of periods. For each period it

  1. predicts the transition potentials if trans_pot_t does not hold them yet, see predict_trans_pot();

  2. builds the allocation context: the anterior map, the allocation-ready potentials (adjusted_trans_pot_v()), the viable transitions, the quantity of change per transition and the allocation parameters;

  3. hands the context to the allocator, which returns the posterior map;

  4. commits the map to lulc_data_t, together with the neighbor predictors the next period is predicted from, in one transaction.

allocate_one_period() runs steps 1-3 for one period and returns the map without committing it. Use it to write your own loop: edit trans_pot_t between prediction and allocation (e.g. theory-driven shifts in potential due to policy interventions), edit the allocated map afterwards, or draw an ensemble of single-period realisations. Commit the map with db$commit(x, "lulc_data_t", method = "upsert") and, if a later period follows, run db$upsert_new_neighbors(id_period_post).

The allocator is one of alloc_clumpy_spec() (stochastic, unbiased; the default), alloc_greedy_spec() (deterministic rank-and-fill) or alloc_dinamica_spec() (Dinamica EGO's expander and patcher).

The quantity of change is the same for every allocator: each viable transition changes round(rate * n_anterior) cells, where rate is the transition's rate in trans_rates_t for the posterior period and n_anterior the number of cells of its anterior class in the anterior map. Transitions without a rate change no cells.

Usage

allocate(
  db,
  id_periods,
  allocator = alloc_clumpy_spec(),
  select_score,
  select_maximize,
  id_run = db$id_run,
  potentials_ancestor = 0L,
  force_predict = FALSE,
  update_neighbors = TRUE
)

allocate_one_period(
  db,
  id_period_post,
  allocator = alloc_clumpy_spec(),
  select_score,
  select_maximize,
  id_run = db$id_run,
  potentials_ancestor = 0L,
  force_predict = FALSE
)

Arguments

db

An evoland_db instance.

id_periods

Integer vector of contiguous posterior period IDs to simulate.

allocator

An allocator specification, see Description.

select_score

Character; mlr3 measure ID (e.g. "classif.auc") used to select the model for prediction, see predict_trans_pot().

select_maximize

Logical; maximize (TRUE) or minimize (FALSE) select_score.

id_run

Integer; the run to allocate. It reads its anterior map, demand and allocation parameters through its lineage, and the allocated maps are written under it.

potentials_ancestor

Integer; how many generations up the lineage of id_run to take the transition potentials from: 0 (default) the run itself, 1 its parent, 2 its grandparent. They are predicted under that run if missing. Use 1 to let sibling runs (e.g. a Monte Carlo ensemble of allocations) share their parent's potentials. 2 only makes sense if the parent's siblings share the same transition potentials too. Above 0 for a single period only: from the second period on, the anterior map is the run's own allocation, which its ancestors cannot see.

force_predict

Logical; if TRUE, predict the transition potentials even if trans_pot_t already holds them for that run and the period.

update_neighbors

Logical; whether to recompute the neighbor predictors after the last period (default TRUE). Intermediate periods are always updated, since the next period's prediction reads them. Set FALSE when nothing is allocated onwards from the last period, e.g. for single-period ensembles.

id_period_post

Integer posterior period ID.

Value

allocate(): called for its side effects on lulc_data_t and pred_data_t; returns NULL invisibly. allocate_one_period(): an lulc_data_t with the posterior map.
